clue.text: Study on prisoner's moral scruples

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
a science is a field of study

explanation.surface: Someone researching an inmate's ethical qualms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like the action, but it is the field of learning; 'on' places it after the convict, and the 's of prisoner's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscience is the inner sense of right and wrong that produces moral scruples.

clue.text: Client's initial request for a barrel

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter, so take the start of Client's

parts.note: to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A customer's first order is for a barrel of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cask is a wooden barrel for holding liquids such as beer or wine.

clue.text: Wanting massage, say, left after four, forgetting regulars

indicators.note: after places the left letter behind the preceding pieces
say signals a word as heard rather than as written

parts.note: to knead is to massage

indicators.note: dropping the regular (even) letters of four leaves its first and third

explanation.surface: Someone craving a rub-down, leaving after four, minus a few regulars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the sound signal on massage; 'forgetting regulars' drops the 2nd and 4th letters of four; 'after' sets L last.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful can mean lacking or in need, the same sense as wanting.

clue.text: Thought given to argument against team allowance

parts.note: the cons are the arguments against, as in pros and cons
a side is a sports team
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: Careful reflection on the case against a squad's allotment.
explanation.definitionFit: Consideration is careful thought given to something.

clue.text: Attractive engineer getting on

parts.note: Eng is an abbreviation for engineer or engineering
getting on means growing old, ageing

explanation.surface: A good-looking engineer who is past their prime.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging means charming and pleasant, so attractive in manner.

clue.text: Caught a kid — what language!

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to kid is to tease, to rib

explanation.surface: Someone catches a youngster swearing and exclaims at the words used.
explanation.definitionFit: Carib is the name of an indigenous language of northern South America.

clue.text: Gangway has top bit missing — land in water!

indicators.note: the first letter of the gangway word is dropped

parts.note: a gangway between seats is an aisle

explanation.surface: A walkway is damaged at the top, and the result floats.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, a piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: The sort of cooking found in prison?

definitions.text: The sort of cooking found in prison?

parts.words: The sort of cooking found in prison?
parts.note: stir is slang for prison, so a fry-up in the stir would be this quick wok method of cooking

explanation.surface: A question about what meals are like inside a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick frying of small pieces while stirring is a cooking method; 'stir' is also slang for jail.

clue.text: One's responsibility to pick members

parts.note: the body of voters is responsible for choosing members of parliament

explanation.surface: A remark about whose job it is to select members of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: The voters in a constituency collectively elect its members of parliament.

clue.text: Forbidding right to wear gun

indicators.note: something worn is surrounded, so the right letter goes inside the gun

parts.note: the Sten was a British sub-machine gun

explanation.surface: It is not permitted to carry a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A stern look is a forbidding, severe one.

clue.text: Miss tour representative — one in uniform?

parts.note: a miss is a young girl
a guide leads a tour

explanation.surface: A young woman working as a holiday rep, perhaps dressed in a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Girl Guides youth movement wears a uniform; the question mark marks this as an example.

clue.text: A one parent gig suffers this, perhaps

definitions.text: A one parent gig suffers this, perhaps

indicators.note: letters that suffer are knocked about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A single parent's performance falls victim to age differences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffers' reorders A ONE PARENT GIG; read as a whole, the clue hints that one parent and child may not see eye to eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The difference in attitudes between young and old people is a familiar source of family friction.

clue.text: The advantage of living on the edge?

definitions.text: The advantage of living on the edge?

parts.words: The advantage of living on the edge?
parts.note: a perk of a job, read literally as the benefit of dwelling at the margin

explanation.surface: Musing on the upside of a life of risk.
explanation.definitionFit: A perk received in addition to salary is an extra advantage; the fringe is also an edge.

clue.text: A fine night represented a favourable set of circumstances

parts.note: fine means good

indicators.note: re-presented means set out again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A pleasant evening reshaped into a lucky situation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something advantageous or beneficial.

clue.text: One's distressed by nerve of attack ships

indicators.note: by places the anagram beside the nerve word

parts.note: gall means nerve, cheek

indicators.note: distressed means damaged and twisted out of shape

parts.note: the letters of One's taken as written, ONES

explanation.surface: Someone upset by the audacity of an assault on shipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' turns ONES into EONS, placed beside GALL; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Galleons were large sailing ships also used as warships.

clue.text: Person forking out to cover traitor's final appeal

indicators.note: the payer word covers, surrounding the final letter

parts.note: someone who forks out pays, a payer

indicators.note: final picks the last letter of traitor's

explanation.surface: Someone paying to shield a traitor's last plea.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer is an earnest appeal or entreaty.

clue.text: He is trapped by company lease — that's logical

indicators.note: the word he is enclosed within the other pieces

parts.note: to rent is to lease
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man caught by his firm's rental agreement, which makes sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Coherent means logical and consistent.

clue.text: The expenditure needed to expose non-professional

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them
lay means not belonging to a profession

explanation.surface: The cost of revealing an amateur.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlay is money spent, an expenditure.

clue.text: Toddlers begin to walk like ducks? Nonsense

indicators.note: begin picks the first letter of toddlers

parts.note: ducks waddle

explanation.surface: Small children start walking in a duck-like way, which is silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is silly talk, nonsense.

clue.text: Most prominent newspaper that's mislaid outside

indicators.note: the lost word sits outside the other pieces

parts.note: something mislaid is lost
FT is the Financial Times newspaper
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A paper that has gone missing gets major billing.
explanation.definitionFit: Loftiest means highest, most elevated, so most prominent.

clue.text: Green's leader worried about source of material

indicators.note: worried means agitated, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: a lead is a leader
re means about, concerning

indicators.note: a source is a starting point, so the first letter of material

explanation.surface: The Green party's head fretting about where some fabric came from.
explanation.walkthrough: Green is the colour, not the party; 'worried' is the anagram signal, and the 's after Green stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerald is a bright green colour.

clue.text: Head into hotel in order to get something to eat

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them afresh

explanation.surface: Instructions to go into a hotel for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: TOAD-IN-THE-HOLE is a British dish of sausages baked in batter.
explanation.definitionFit: This dish of sausages in Yorkshire pudding batter is a meal to eat.

clue.text: Short uprising followed by ultimately fragile ceasefire

indicators.note: followed by sets the next piece after
in a down clue an uprising reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: curt means short, brusque

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of fragile

explanation.surface: A brief revolt ends in a shaky armistice.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is an agreement to stop fighting, a ceasefire.

clue.text: Bits of garden furniture?

parts.note: planted plots are parts of a garden, and things to sleep on are furniture

explanation.surface: A question about outdoor chairs and tables.
explanation.definitionFit: Flower plots are parts of a garden, and the same word names items of bedroom furniture.

clue.text: Apprentice's agreement produced one new plate

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a dental plate is a denture

explanation.surface: Someone made a fresh dental plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An indenture is the contract binding an apprentice to a master.

clue.text: Look around the back of larder and eat

indicators.note: the look word goes around the picked letter

parts.note: to gaze is to look

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Peering about the rear of the pantry and then eating.
explanation.definitionFit: To graze is to eat, especially in snacks or as animals feed on grass.

clue.text: Here, El Greco returned full of joy

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
the phrase Here, El Greco is full of the letters, holding them across its word breaks

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A painter arrives back and is delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'full of joy' as definition, leaving the hidden run with no indicator; 'full of' is that indicator, and 'joy' alone defines the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is great delight, a synonym of joy.

clue.text: Insects' reported smell prevents male going

indicators.note: reported signals a word as spoken

parts.note: a scent is a smell

indicators.note: going means the male letter departs

parts.note: impedes means hinders, prevents

explanation.surface: An odour that hinders men from leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: SCENT sounds like CENT; IMPEDES without M gives IPEDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Centipedes are many-legged arthropods, loosely called insects; the possessive is a link ('is').
